title: GC-201 Tablet Compression: Weight Variance — Operator Retrained, Root Cause Closed

grill_input.process_step: Tablet Compression (Rotary Press, Equipment ID: RP-04)
grill_input.description_what_happened: During routine in-process weight check at compression, 47 tablets out of 500 sampled fell outside specification (target 50 ± 2 mg; range observed 47.8–52.3 mg). Batch was held and 100% sorted. Root cause investigation concluded operator error in hopper feed rate adjustment.
grill_input.description_what_should_have_happened: All tablets compressed to 50 ± 2 mg per SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 4. Operator should have maintained hopper feed rate at 'Position 3' throughout run.
grill_input.document_deviated_from: SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 4, Section 4.2.1: 'Set hopper feed rate dial to Position 3 before starting compression cycle. Do not adjust during run.'
grill_input.immediate_corrections: Batch GC201-2024-04521 sorted 100%; 453 conforming tablets retained, 47 non-conforming tablets destroyed. Equipment RP-04 cleaned and re-qualified. Operator (ID: OP-2847) removed from compression line pending retraining.
investigation_steps: Visual inspection of RP-04 hopper and feed mechanism: no mechanical defects noted.
Review of operator logbook: operator OP-2847 noted 'adjusted feed dial twice during run due to inconsistent tablet weight.' No record of why adjustment was deemed necessary.

Interview with operator OP-2847: stated 'I thought the tablets were coming out light, so I moved the dial to Position 4 midway through. Then I moved it back to Position 3 when I saw heavier tablets.' Operator acknowledged not following SOP step 4.2.1.
No review of hopper calibration or feed rate verification data.
No comparison with other operators' runs on same equipment.
grill_input.root_cause_description: Operator OP-2847 deviated from SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 4, Section 4.2.1 by adjusting the hopper feed rate dial during the compression run without authorization. This caused inconsistent tablet weight. Root cause: operator did not follow written procedure.
grill_input.impact_assessment: Batch GC201-2024-04521 (10,000 tablets): 47 tablets (0.47%) out of specification. No tablets released to market. No patient impact. Batch disposition: 453 conforming tablets released after 100% sort; 47 non-conforming tablets destroyed.

capa.description: Retraining of operator OP-2847 on SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 4, Section 4.2.1. Operator to complete classroom training and supervised compression run (minimum 2 hours) before return to independent operation.

statements.speaker: Operator OP-2847
statements.quote: I adjusted the dial because the tablets looked light coming out. The SOP says not to adjust, but I thought I was helping quality.

statements.speaker: Line Supervisor (LS-0412)
statements.quote: Operator OP-2847 told me the hopper was jamming and feed was inconsistent, which is why they adjusted. But they never reported it formally.

case_packet.true_systemic_cause: SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 4, Section 4.2.1 is ambiguous and operationally unworkable at line speed. The step reads 'Set hopper feed rate dial to Position 3 before starting compression cycle. Do not adjust during run.' However, the hopper feed rate dial has no detent or lock mechanism; it drifts under vibration. Additionally, the SOP does not define what 'Position 3' means numerically or how to verify it is set correctly. Operators trained on Rev 3 (superseded 6 months prior) were taught to 'monitor and micro-adjust the dial every 5 minutes to maintain consistent feed.' Rev 4 removed this instruction without explanation, creating cognitive conflict. Operator OP-2847 was trained on Rev 3 and never formally re-trained on Rev 4; they received only a 'read and sign' email notice of the change.
case_packet.hopper_calibration_history: Equipment RP-04 hopper feed mechanism was last calibrated 18 months ago. Calibration certificate shows dial position drift of ±0.3 units under normal vibration. No recalibration scheduled. Maintenance logs show 'hopper vibration' complaints from 4 operators in the past 8 months, none escalated.
case_packet.other_operator_feedback: Interviews with operators OP-1923, OP-2104, and OP-3341 (conducted post-closure, not in original investigation) reveal: all three have adjusted the feed dial during runs; all three state the dial 'creeps' and tablets become inconsistent if not monitored; all three were trained on Rev 3 and did not receive formal training on Rev 4; all three assumed Rev 4 was a 'read-only' notice and continued prior practice.
case_packet.sop_revision_history: SOP GC-201-COMP-012 Rev 3 (effective 2023-08-15): Section 4.2.1 stated 'Set hopper feed rate dial to Position 3 (marked line) before starting. Monitor dial every 5 minutes and adjust ±0.1 units if feed inconsistency observed.' Rev 4 (effective 2023-10-01): Section 4.2.1 changed to 'Set hopper feed rate dial to Position 3 before starting compression cycle. Do not adjust during run.' Change rationale in change control CC-2023-1847: 'Simplify procedure to reduce operator variability.' No risk assessment of removing the monitoring step. No operator feedback solicited.
case_packet.training_records: Operator OP-2847: Last formal training on compression procedures was 2023-07-20 (Rev 3 curriculum). Email notice of SOP Rev 4 sent 2023-10-01 with subject 'SOP Update — Read and Acknowledge.' OP-2847 acknowledged receipt 2023-10-02 but did not complete any hands-on retraining. No record of supervisor verification that OP-2847 understood the change.
case_packet.maintenance_work_order: WO-2024-0156 (dated 2024-01-28, 2 weeks before deviation): Operator complaint 'hopper feed dial drifts during run, causing weight variation.' Maintenance response: 'Dial position verified at 0.2 units drift. Recommend recalibration.' Recommendation not acted upon; no follow-up scheduled.
case_packet.effectiveness_check_status: CAPA-2024-0847-001 (retraining) was marked complete on 2024-03-08. No effectiveness verification conducted. No follow-up compression runs monitored. No audit of other operators' adherence to Rev 4 performed.
case_packet.conflicting_statement_resolution: Line Supervisor LS-0412's statement about 'hopper jamming' is supported by maintenance WO-2024-0156 and operator feedback. Operator OP-2847 did not formally report the issue, but the condition was real and known to maintenance. Operator's adjustment was a rational response to a latent system defect, not willful non-compliance.
